scope: Foundational reconstruction of living organization, compartments, metabolism, inheritance, evolution, gene and genome organization, protein structure and function, cell processes, development, organismal physiology, population ecology, and biological evidence boundaries.
exclusions: molecular identity already owned by Chemistry is cited rather than rederived
clinical intervention and efficacy belong to Medicine and Health Sciences
consciousness and qualia belong to the Consciousness branch
engineering implementation and Fold Protein remain downstream application work
future biological discoveries remain lawful extensions after independent admission

obligations.title: Living organization
obligations.statement: Living organization is a bounded process network that retains its identity by regulated material and energy turnover within a declared viability window.

obligations.title: Living and nonliving chemical-network boundary
obligations.statement: A chemical network is biologically living only when compartment, maintenance, heritable continuation and regulated resource exchange are jointly retained; chemistry alone does not supply that classification.

obligations.title: Autocatalytic closure and origin-of-life boundary
obligations.statement: Autocatalytic closure is the least complete finite reaction support in which every required catalytic role is regenerated by the network while resources and boundary conditions remain explicit.

obligations.title: Biological maintenance
obligations.statement: Maintenance is the generated set of transitions that restores identity-defining biological relations faster than incompatible distinctions accumulate at the declared boundary.

obligations.title: Identity through constituent turnover
obligations.statement: Biological identity persists through constituent replacement exactly when the lineage-bound organization and its required transition relations remain reconstructible.

obligations.title: Loss of living closure
obligations.statement: Biological death is the condition-bounded loss of the jointly required maintenance, regulation and integrated continuation relations, not numerical zero or disappearance of material.

obligations.title: Biological compartment
obligations.statement: A biological compartment is a connected boundary that retains distinguishable internal and external content classes together with every permitted transfer path.

obligations.title: Inside/outside orientation
obligations.statement: A retained compartment boundary forces two held side labels, inside and outside, whose distinction cannot be erased by a lawful transfer description.

obligations.title: Membrane organization
obligations.statement: A membrane is a continuous oriented component organization that maintains a compartment while retaining composition, adjacency, state and interruption records.

obligations.title: Selective permeability
obligations.statement: Selective permeability is the complete partition of candidate boundary crossings into permitted and rejected species-state paths under declared conditions.

obligations.title: Nested biological compartments
obligations.statement: Nested biological organization is a finite containment tree in which every compartment boundary, side label and cross-boundary transfer remains separately reconstructible.

obligations.title: Compartment lineage provenance
obligations.statement: Compartment identity claims require an unbroken predecessor-to-successor record across division, fusion, growth and component turnover.

obligations.title: Metabolic network
obligations.statement: Metabolism is a compartment-bound transformation network that records every resource, product, catalyst, transfer and retained constituent relation required for maintenance.

obligations.title: Biological resource uptake
obligations.statement: Resource uptake is a source-bound permitted transition from an external support into a biological compartment with identity, amount, route and condition retained.

obligations.title: Metabolic transformation conservation
obligations.statement: A metabolic transformation is admissible only when the complete constituent ledger balances and catalysts, resources and products remain separately identified.

obligations.title: Metabolic process coupling
obligations.statement: Biological process coupling joins otherwise nonpersistent and resource-releasing transitions through one retained transfer record; an unrecorded gain is rejected.

obligations.title: Metabolic by-product and waste export
obligations.statement: Waste export is a recorded transfer of nonretained metabolic products across the compartment boundary; no product may disappear from the constituent ledger.

obligations.title: Finite biological resource closure
obligations.statement: Resource closure is always relative to a declared organism-environment boundary and finite interval and requires every necessary input, transformation, storage, export and loss path to be recorded.

obligations.title: Information-bearing inheritance
obligations.statement: Inheritance is the reconstructible retention of a biological distinction from predecessor to successor through an identified carrier and generation relation.

obligations.title: Template-directed copying
obligations.statement: Template copying generates a product word through a declared positionwise relation while retaining template, product, direction and every mismatch.

obligations.title: Biological replication
obligations.statement: Replication is a resource-bounded process that generates at least one distinct successor carrying the declared hereditary relation while retaining predecessor and copy provenance.

obligations.title: Replication fidelity and error
obligations.statement: Copy fidelity is the exact part-to-whole count of agreed positions over a declared aligned word; every mismatch and unobserved position remains in the record.

obligations.title: Heritable copy variation
obligations.statement: A copy difference is heritable variation only when its exact state and location persist through a registered successor relation rather than appearing only as transient damage or observation error.

obligations.title: Replication lineage
obligations.statement: A replication lineage is a finite directed predecessor-successor graph with every sampled branch, merger, missing observation and generation boundary explicit.

obligations.title: Biological variation
obligations.statement: Variation is the complete retained set of distinguishable biological states within a declared population and sampling boundary.

obligations.title: Heritability relation
obligations.statement: Heritability is a population- and condition-bounded relation between predecessor and successor distinctions and does not by itself identify a molecular cause.

obligations.title: Differential reproduction
obligations.statement: Differential reproduction is an exact comparison of retained successor counts among biological types under one declared environment and generation window.

obligations.title: Selection
obligations.statement: Selection is the recurrence of a heritable variant together with reproducible differential continuation relative to registered alternatives under a declared environment.

obligations.title: Fixation and loss boundary
obligations.statement: Fixation is whole support of one retained variant in the declared population; loss is structural absence of that variant from the same support, never a universal guarantee from benefit alone.

obligations.title: Selection and drift distinction
obligations.statement: A change is attributed to selection only when the registered variant-continuation relation survives the declared controls; otherwise finite sampling recurrence remains an explicit drift-compatible alternative.

obligations.title: Nucleic-acid symbol alphabet
obligations.statement: Two independent held distinctions generate exactly four nucleic-acid symbol labels at the DNA coding boundary.

obligations.title: Triplet codon word space
obligations.statement: Three ordered positions over four generated symbols force exactly sixty-four distinguishable codon words.

obligations.title: First-two-position codon boxes
obligations.statement: The sixty-four codons partition by their first two positions into exactly sixteen boxes of exactly four third-position words each.

obligations.title: Gene as expression-bearing hereditary interval
obligations.statement: A gene is a source-bound hereditary interval whose expression or regulatory relation is demonstrated with orientation, context and evidence boundary retained.

obligations.title: Genome organization
obligations.statement: A genome is the complete declared hereditary carrier support of an organism or cell with order, linkage, compartment, copy state, gaps and assembly provenance retained.

obligations.title: Expression and regulation
obligations.statement: Gene expression is a recorded transition from a hereditary interval to a product; regulation is a reproducible condition-dependent difference in that transition with regulator, context and time retained.

obligations.title: Protein sequence identity
obligations.statement: A protein sequence is an ordered residue word with every position, linkage, modification, ambiguity and source record retained.

obligations.title: Protein folding relation
obligations.statement: Protein folding is a condition-bounded transition from sequence support to a recurrent structural class; it is a generated descent relation, not exhaustive random search or an imported unique-shape premise.

obligations.title: Protein conformational ensemble
obligations.statement: A protein state is an observed recurrence class over a conformational ensemble; one structure may not erase retained alternate conformations or intrinsically disordered support.

obligations.title: Protein function
obligations.statement: Protein function is a reproducible protein-dependent difference in a declared biological process under explicit context and controls, not a label inferred from shape alone.

obligations.title: Protein interaction
obligations.statement: A protein interaction is a reproducible specific joint-state relation whose alternatives, stoichiometry, condition and observation method are retained.

obligations.title: Quaternary protein assembly
obligations.statement: Quaternary assembly is a generated multi-chain joint state that retains chain identities, stoichiometry, symmetry, interface contacts and adverse steric alternatives; no fitted docking score may select it.

obligations.title: Biological homochirality
obligations.statement: Biological homochirality is a source-bound recurrence of one molecular hand across a declared biopolymer class; Chemistry supplies chirality while Biology owns its lineage-maintained selection.

obligations.title: Cell identity
obligations.statement: A cell is the least compartmented living organization jointly retaining boundary, maintenance, hereditary continuation and regulated process integration.

obligations.title: Cellular transport
obligations.statement: Cellular transport is a counted species-state transition through a declared membrane route with direction, driving relation and intracellular fate retained.

obligations.title: Cell signalling
obligations.statement: Cell signalling is a reconstructible source-to-receptor-to-response transition chain whose intermediates, controls, timing and alternative routes remain explicit.

obligations.title: Excitable-cell threshold transition
obligations.statement: An excitable-cell event is a regenerative state transition after a declared threshold is crossed, distinguished from subthreshold and refractory responses; no universal voltage is imported.

obligations.title: Cell division
obligations.statement: Cell division partitions one lineage-bound cell into successor compartments while retaining the complete hereditary, cytoplasmic, boundary and error-allocation record.

obligations.title: Dysregulated cell continuation and cancer boundary
obligations.statement: Dysregulated cellular continuation is a lineage-supported failure of normal division, death or differentiation control under a declared tissue context; cycling alone is not sufficient to identify cancer.

obligations.title: Multicellular organismal composition
obligations.statement: Multicellular organization is a connected lineage-related cell composition with retained cellular identities and regulated shared processes.

obligations.title: Cell adhesion and tissue boundary
obligations.statement: Cell adhesion is a specific persistent intercellular or cell-matrix relation that retains component identity, contact geometry, mechanical context and adverse controls.

obligations.title: Cell differentiation
obligations.statement: Differentiation is a stable lineage-related divergence of cellular state and function while hereditary carrier identity and transition provenance remain reconstructible.

obligations.title: Developmental lineage
obligations.statement: Development is an ordered lineage of division, movement and differentiation transitions from an initiating cell to a multicellular organization with every branch and stage boundary retained.

obligations.title: Morphogenesis
obligations.statement: Morphogenesis is the reconstruction of global biological form from local cell-state, adjacency, movement and boundary transitions over a declared developmental interval.

obligations.title: Biological regeneration
obligations.statement: Regeneration is a lineage-supported transition from a recorded loss state to restored organization and function, with residual source, path, extent and failures retained.

obligations.title: Organism identity
obligations.statement: An organism is an integrated lineage-bound living whole whose parts participate in coordinated maintenance, development, reproduction or continuation within a declared life cycle.

obligations.title: Physiological process
obligations.statement: Physiology is the complete coordinated transition record by which organismal parts maintain or change a biological function under declared conditions.

obligations.title: Homeostatic regulation
obligations.statement: Homeostasis is a closed sensing-and-response recurrence that returns a biological variable to a declared viable range while preserving delays, overshoot and failure cases.

obligations.title: Organismal reproduction
obligations.statement: Organismal reproduction generates a new lineage-bound organism through declared parental carrier contributions and development, with variation and failures retained.

obligations.title: Biological life cycle
obligations.statement: A biological life cycle is the complete ordered recurrence of organismal stages including development, reproductive continuation and terminal loss at a declared taxonomic boundary.

obligations.title: Senescence and longevity
obligations.statement: Senescence is an age-linked change in maintenance or continuation measured on a declared lineage and population; longevity requires survival and censoring records and is not forced by denominator parity alone.

obligations.title: Biological population
obligations.statement: A population is a declared set of organismal individuals connected by place, time and relevant biological interaction, with membership and sampling rules explicit.

obligations.title: Species and reproductive boundary
obligations.statement: A species claim is an explicitly chosen, evidence-bound equivalence class over populations; reproductive, phylogenetic and ecological criteria may not be silently merged.

obligations.title: Ecological community
obligations.statement: A community is a place- and time-bounded network of distinguishable populations and their observed interactions, including absent and unresolved links.

obligations.title: Trophic and resource network
obligations.statement: A trophic network is a directed resource-transfer graph retaining source, consumer, amount basis, direction, loss and observation boundary for every edge.

obligations.title: Ecosystem organization
obligations.statement: An ecosystem is a bounded joint organization of communities and abiotic supports with complete registered stocks, transfers, losses and observation history.

obligations.title: Ecological recurrence and stability
obligations.statement: Ecological recurrence is a return of a complete declared state class; stability is persistence or recovery under registered perturbations and cannot be inferred from one bounded-denominator orbit alone.

obligations.title: Ecological network topology
obligations.statement: Ecological network topology is the exact degree, path and clustering census of a declared interaction graph; scale-free or small-world labels require whole-graph and unfavorable-model comparison.

obligations.title: Biological allometric relation
obligations.statement: A biological allometric claim is a population-bounded comparison of trait and body-size recurrence with taxa, stages, conditions, residuals and alternative exponents retained; no universal exponent is imported.

obligations.title: Biological specimen and sampling
obligations.statement: A biological specimen is a finite source-bound part with collection, preservation, preparation, subsampling and representativeness boundaries explicit.

obligations.title: Biological condition and control
obligations.statement: A biological comparison requires experimental units, conditions, controls, timing and context to be registered before the outcome is opened.

obligations.title: Biological assay
obligations.statement: A biological assay is a specimen-bound observation process with calibration, detection, processing, exclusions and method-validity boundaries retained.

obligations.title: Biological uncertainty and missingness
obligations.statement: Biological evidence must retain biological variation, measurement error, missingness, censoring and unresolved states rather than collapsing them into one favorable estimate.

obligations.title: Biological causal and associative boundary
obligations.statement: A biological causal claim requires a registered intervention or adequate control structure that eliminates generated alternatives; association alone remains explicitly noncausal.

obligations.title: Cross-branch biological handoff
obligations.statement: A Biology claim cites upstream mathematical, informational, physical, chemical and material laws without reowning them and exports organismal consequences without claiming medical efficacy, consciousness or engineering implementation.
